Nigel Farage adviser had unpublicised role at polling firm
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:42:27 UTC
22:42:27 KST

A close adviser to Nigel Farage had an influential role at a national polling company despite not being publicly associated with the firm, the Guardian can reveal.
Chris Bruni-Lowe, Farage’s private pollster for many years, played an important role in the operations of Redfield & Wilton Strategies and used it to develop potential campaign strategies, according to several sources who have worked there.
The firm, founded in 2020, is owned by Bruno Rodrigues, a lawyer. Its main public face was Philip van Scheltinga, a Harvard graduate.
As the Covid pandemic grew and the UK entered lockdown, the company’s polls received increasing coverage, even while the source of the firm’s polling expertise was unclear. Former employees have now revealed the important role of Bruni-Lowe, who sometimes went by the name “Chris Redfield”, under which quotes were published by the Washington Post newspaper.
As well as ordering UK and US voter intention polls, sources said Bruni-Lowe directed research on issues such as council spending, and appeared “obsessed” with producing a dossier which he suggested could be sold to political parties.
Bruni-Lowe’s role at the company will amplify questions about transparency in the polling industry, given his longstanding association with Farage at a time of intense scrutiny over the party’s use of polls to shape its political narrative.
The rules of the British Polling Council do not require pollsters to state any political affiliations, but they have strict guidelines on how they must declare who has commissioned and paid for any polling.
In a statement, Rodrigues, the company’s sole director, said there had never been “an institutional, polling, research, commissioning or financial relationship” between Redfield & Wilton and Reform UK or Farage.
He said Bruni-Lowe had worked as a “consultant” from mid-2020 until late 2022, and returned “voluntarily” in the summer of 2025 to train interns. Rodrigues added that Bruni-Lowe was “an important and highly valued member” of the team.
Sources said Bruni-Lowe, who some employees said had been known as “Chris Redfield”, was heavily involved in the company’s polling operations.
Rodrigues said the surname Redfield was used as an email account convention within the organisation, citing other examples of “Philip Redfield” and “Bruno Redfield”. He said: “It was not a device created specifically for Chris and it did not conceal his identity from people working within the company.”
Nonetheless, the situation was confusing enough that at least one newspaper, the Washington Post, attributed quotes to that name, while notes taken by one former employee during an oral induction in the summer of 2021, and seen by the Guardian, described “boss – Chris Redfield is COO essentially”.
Rodrigues said: “He was never presented to staff as the company’s chief operating officer and staff were never instructed to treat him as such.” He added that Van Scheltinga, as director of research, led the “day-to-day operation”.
The Guardian can also reveal that Dan Jukes, then a senior adviser to Farage, sought to promote Redfield & Wilton’s work in 2020, looking to place exclusive polls in publications including the Guardian, which turned down the offer.
Jukes stepped down as Farage’s chief of staff recently over a scandal in which undercover reporters posed as potential overseas donors to Reform UK. Footage published by Channel 4 News showed the co-founder of polling firm JL Partners, James Johnson, apparently acknowledging that Jukes had commissioned polling funded by an overseas donor.
The polling had appeared in newspapers without any reference to the party, with JL Partners acknowledging “weaknesses” in its procedures.
Jukes denies wrongdoing and Reform UK has said the party itself did not commission the work. On Wednesday, Reform announced that an internal inquiry had cleared the officials of breaking the law. The matter remains under police investigation.
Redfield & Wilton started producing polls in 2020 with little information about the people behind the company. During its publicly active years before it became less visible in late 2024, its voter intention polls frequently appeared in politically influential newsletters from Politico, the Times, and the New Statesman.
Bruni-Lowe ran Farage’s 2015 election campaign, helped test messaging for the formation of the Brexit party and advised on the 2019 local elections campaign, as well as having produced private polling for Farage since at least 2014, apart from during a brief period of working for Rishi Sunak before the 2024 election. In his book on political strategy, he writes of having worked for “organisations and candidates of all political persuasions”.
He is considered to be part of Farage’s inner circle and was close enough to the Reform UK leader to have been present on a trip to party donor Christopher Harborne’s Thai wellness retreat at Christmas in 2022 to mark the crypto billionaire’s 60th birthday.
Other guests photographed at the meeting include Farage’s unpaid aide and convicted fraudster George Cottrell.
In May 2023, Van Scheltinga and Bruni-Lowe were photographed having drinks at a Mayfair restaurant with Farage, Cottrell and Richard Tice, the Reform UK deputy leader.
Rodrigues said: “The existence of personal or social meetings involving individuals associated with the company does not establish a corporate relationship between Redfield & Wilton Strategies and Reform UK.”
While much of Redfield & Wilton’s published polling related to voter intentions in the UK and the US, sources said Bruni-Lowe had its staff develop a “dossier” on local authority performance between autumn 2024 and spring 2025.
One source said he suggested the firm’s work could be sold to political parties, and that Bruni-Lowe appeared “obsessed” with the dossier. Research by employees included freedom of information requests to councils to find expenditure on translation services.
Rodrigues said the FOI project was a “commercial research project” and translation services were just one of “several dozen categories” examined by the company in a project led by Van Scheltinga. He added that none of the research was supplied to Reform or Farage.
The company’s other work, sources said, included polling in Montenegro, Hungary, Hong Kong and the Bahamas, as well as research about attitudes in the UK to gold and cryptocurrencies.
Employees were not always told exactly how their work would be used. According to one former employee, they were told their work on a foreign election would be for the Telegraph, but the polling never appeared in the newspaper. Another said they believed their work on cryptocurrencies was for a client.
One unusual piece of work by the company was an October 2021 submission to an inquiry into central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) carried out by the House of Lords economic affairs committee. The company cited polling it said “was self-funded internally by Redfield & Wilton Strategies Ltd for the purpose of this submission”.
The submission said the scepticism of the British public over the UK government’s capacity for innovation meant “it is strategically important that alternatives to a CBDC from the private sector, including those that are already in use, are also given the opportunity to be developed further”.
According to a person who worked at the company at the time of the submission, “all of the crypto stuff came down from Chris [Bruni-Lowe]”.
One online profile for Rodrigues, a solicitor based in London, refers to him holding a directorship of an “innovative market research firm”. However, according to former employees, he had a limited role in the day-to-day running of Redfield & Wilton. One source said that at a rare in-person meeting Rodrigues was “paraded around on a laptop on a Zoom call”.
Van Scheltinga was frequently quoted giving analysis of the company’s polling and wrote columns for the Times and Telegraph.
Van Scheltinga was the listed contact for the company with the British Polling Council, the trade body for pollsters, but one industry source said he never attended BPC meetings. This led to demands from the BPC for a representative of the group to appear before them: that was ultimately Rodrigues, the nominal director, who maintained “total silence”, according to the industry source.
Bruni-Lowe declined to comment. Van Scheltinga did not respond to requests for comment.

Fire destroys Marché des Enfants Rouges, ‘coolest market in Paris’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:41:21 UTC
22:41:21 KST

Fire has ravaged Paris’s oldest surviving covered food market, a popular street food venue dating back to the 17th century in the Marais district of the French capital that drew thousands of locals and tourists daily.
Ariel Weil, the central Paris mayor, said the Marché des Enfants Rouges had been “totally destroyed” in the blaze, which broke out soon after 3am. “The worst was avoided: the fire did not spread to the surrounding buildings,” he said. “But there is a lot of emotion. A lot of sadness.”
The market was established in 1615 during the reign of Louis XIII and took its name from a nearby orphanage, the Hospice des Enfants Rouges – founded in 1536 by King Francis I and his sister Marguerite de Navarre – whose child residents were habitually dressed in red.
The structure was listed as a historic monument in 1982 but narrowly escaped demolition shortly afterwards when Paris city hall, led by the then mayor, Jacques Chirac, approved radical redevelopment plans that would have replaced it with an underground car park, a council daycare facility and community centre.
A determined campaign by local residents and neighbourhood associations, backed by intellectuals, writers and artists including film-makers and photographers such as Bertrand Tavernier and Willy Ronis, who captured its traders on camera, gathered tens of thousands of signatures in protest and the plans were eventually abandoned in the mid-1990s.
Rather than demolish the building, the city undertook a six-year, 13m-franc (about €3m, or £2.5m today) renovation project, restoring the market’s historic wood and ironwork frame and glass roof. Les Enfants Rouges reopened as a food court in 2000.
While still hosting some traditional stalls including a greengrocer, butcher, cheesemonger and fishmonger, the 1,000 sq m market was mostly given over to more than a dozen stands offering French, Lebanese, Moroccan, Japanese and other street food at the counter or at casual chairs and tables.
The current Time Out tourist guide describes Les Enfants Rouges as “the coolest market in Paris”, while the authoritative US website Food&Wine ranked it fifth worldwide for street food this year after other food courts in London, Bangkok, Lyon and Mexico City.
Lt Col Pierre de Bouvier of the Paris fire service said much of the metal structure of the market had fallen in, and most of the stalls had gone up in flames. More than 150 firefighters and 50 fire trucks battled the blaze after being alerted at 4.15am, he said, adding that the cause of the fire was not yet known.

EU considers issuing Russian tourists Schengen visas valid only in certain territories

EU considers issuing Russian tourists Schengen visas valid only in certain territories
The agenda for an EU Council working group meeting on visa policy includes a proposal to issue Russian nationals visas with limited territorial validity.
The document says the issue is whether to issue Russian citizens so-called LTV visas (Limited Territorial Validity) for “non-essential travel,” including tourism. The working group is scheduled to meet on October 14.
LTV visas, which allow travel only to certain countries rather than the full Schengen area, are already being issued. It remains unclear whether the working group plans to discuss issuing Russians only these visas.
Representatives of Russia’s tourism industry note that issuing Russians only LTV visas would significantly complicate organizing multi-country bus routes and combined trips to several states in a single journey.
Politico previously reported that the EU plans to introduce new visa restrictions for Russians starting in 2027, with the issue also set for discussion October 12 at a meeting of the EU Foreign Affairs Council. Several EU countries cite the threat of hybrid attacks from Russia as the reason for tightening visa policy. The report did not specify what the new restrictions would entail.
Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on October 11 that fully halting the issuance of tourist visas to Russians is necessary to strengthen Europe’s security. The Finnish prime minister plans to submit the proposal at the EU summit on October 15–16.
Finland, like a number of other EU and Schengen Area countries, stopped issuing tourist visas to Russians shortly after the start of Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine.
However, some other countries, including Greece, Spain, Italy, and France, continue to issue tourist visas to Russian citizens. In 2025, according to data cited by Politico, around 478,000 Schengen tourist visas were issued to Russian citizens.
In November 2025, the European Commission recommended not issuing multiple-entry Schengen visas to Russians. The number of such visas has dropped sharply, but some are still being issued.

Why are the Houthis attacking Saudi airports and how are the missiles getting through?

22:41:17 KST

Explainer Why are the Houthis attacking Saudi airports and how are the missiles getting through? Attacks by Iran-backed group come amid counteroffensive by Yemeni government supported by Riyadh What happened over the weekend? On Saturday, a missile strike by the Houthis in Yemen hit Riyadh’s international airport, killing 13 people and wounding hundreds. On Sunday, another attack killed one person and injured nearly a dozen others. CCTV footage showed people cowering at the moment of impact of Saturday’s attack. CCTV from inside Riyadh airport shows moment of deadly airstrike Footage filmed in the aftermath of showed damage inside one of the terminal buildings at the airport, which is located about 22 miles north of the Saudi Arabian capital. Aftermath of strike on Riyadh’s international airport The attacks by the Houthis, an Iran-backed group, were the biggest escalation yet in their campaign against Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in recent weeks. View image in fullscreen Smoke rising from the site of the Saudi Aramco refinery south of Riyadh on 3 October after a suspect Houthi attack. Photograph: European Union/Copernicus Sentinel-3/Reuters Though the violence might appear at first sight to be restricted to the Arabian peninsula, it could have global consequences, pushing up fuel prices and so international inflation. Why now? The Houthis’ timing is partly opportunistic but also rooted in the dynamics of the conflicts across the Gulf. The Houthis initially stayed on the sidelines of the conflict launched by the US and Israel against Iran earlier this year. But last month, the Islamist militia movement seized control of key territory and gained virtual control of the Bab al-Mandab strait, which dominates the Red Sea, a critical shipping route for oil and gas exports from the region. View image in fullscreen A satellite view of Mayun island, also known as Perim island, in the Bab al-Mandeb strait. Photograph: Planet Labs Inc./AP The Yemeni government forces and local allies began a major counteroffensive last week to drive back the Houthis from the Bab al-Mandab and also hit other Houthi positions. Saudi Arabia is in the Houthis’ crosshairs because it supports Yemen’s UN-backed government and its forces. Their attacks on high-profile targets in the kingdom such as oil infrastructure and the capital’s airport – key symbols of its international integration and economic future – makes painfully obvious the costs of Riyadh’s strategic choices. map of attacked airports in Saudi Arabia Such attacks also benefits Iran, which has long supported the Houthis as part of its “axis of resistance”, a coalition of Islamist hardline movements that allows Tehran to project power and influence round the region. The new threat from the Houthis to the Red Sea and to Saudi Arabia highlights again the massive leverage Tehran and its allies can exert on global oil and gas supplies, countering recent US pressure in bold move on the conflict’s chessboard. How is this new territory for Saudi Arabia? The recent attacks on Saudi Arabia have been the deadliest to hit the kingdom in a decade. They also marked one of the most significant disruptions to Saudi civil aviation in years, forcing airlines across Europe and Asia to suspend services. Businesses in Riyadh’s financial hub have told employees to work remotely, authorities in Riyadh have asked schools to switch to online classes this week, and top energy executives were dropped from the schedule of a high-profile conference this week in the capital. View image in fullscreen A screengrab from a video showing a fire at King Khalid international airport in Riyadh on Thursday 8 October. Photograph: AP Though Saudi Arabia has intervened indirectly in conflicts around the Middle East and beyond for decades, violence has rarely struck the kingdom itself. In recent months, the country has found itself on a frontline, something its rulers have long sought to avoid. Why couldn’t Riyadh stop the missiles? Saudi Arabia has invested enormous sums in its military – the kingdom is the world’s eighth biggest spender on weapons – but Houthi attacks are very hard to stop. “Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves,” said Thomas Juneau, a security analyst at Ottawa University. Other analysts point out that even the vaunted Israeli air defence systems failed to stop a ballistic missile narrowly missing Ben Gurion international airport last year. Reprisals against the Houthis and efforts to pre-emptively destroy the movement’s offensive capabilities are not easy either. The US bombardment in 2025 showed how hard it is to destroy the militia’s capabilities, which have been much enhanced over recent years, in part through Iranian advice and investment. What might happen next? The Houthis say their actions were “guided by reciprocity” – suggesting they are responding to ongoing Saudi strikes on the territory they control in Yemen – but show no sign of stopping their attacks. “Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing,” official statements carried by the Houthi-run al-Masirah television channel said. It seems unlikely Saudi Arabia will halt its counterstrikes, and equally unlikely the kingdom will be able to find a way to block all incoming Houthi missiles, though it may improve its intelligence gathering and early warning to allow better defence of specific high-value targets. View image in fullscreen The aftermath of a Saudi airstrike on a factory in Houthi-controlled Sana’a on 9 October. Photograph: Mohammed Huwais/AFP/Getty Images Nor is there any imminent prospect of an end to the hostilities between Iran and the US that are a major factor in the surge of the recent violence in Yemen. And though the Houthis are more a coalition of different factions than a coherent single movement, for the moment they appear unified behind hardline and ideologically committed leaders. Farea al-Muslimi, a specialist on Yemen and the Gulf at Chatham House in London, said the Houthis had been consistently underestimated over the years. “They have really upped their game and believe they can get something now which will reposition them within the region. They are very confident at the moment and feeling empowered …. But though they think they can control this [escalation], that may well be an illusion,” he said. Unknown Publisher

16:40:26 EEST

The SBU blocked the registration of more than 10 Starlinks for Russians: 4 suspects detained
Kyiv • UNN
The SBU detained four suspects for registering and activating Starlink terminals for Russians. They face life imprisonment with confiscation of property.
Employees of the Security Service of Ukraine blocked new attempts to register Starlink satellite terminals for armed groups of the Russian Federation. This was reported by the SBU press center, according to UNN.
Details
In Khmelnytskyi region, SBU counterintelligence officers detained a mobilized serviceman who had voluntarily deserted his military unit and, on orders from the Russian Federation, registered 10 satellite terminals. Hiding in Kamianets-Podilskyi, he sold the Russian security officer the details obtained to activate the Starlinks.
In Zaporizhzhia, a local unemployed man was detained "red-handed" after activating Starlinks for Russians in the temporarily occupied territories of Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia regions. To verify the terminals, the suspect involved his acquaintances, promising them money while concealing the identity of the customer from the aggressor country.
In Mykolaiv region, two residents of the regional center were exposed at once, one of whom had previously been prosecuted for robbery.
The suspects registered satellite terminals through postal operators’ services, using the details of front persons. In this way, they activated more than 10 devices for the Russians.
All those detained were notified that they were suspected under Part 2 of Article 111 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine (high treason committed under martial law). All the suspects are currently in custody; they face life imprisonment with confiscation of property.
Recall
In Rivne, a student from Kyiv was detained on suspicion of preparing a terrorist attack on orders from Russian intelligence services. According to the investigation, he planted explosives under a bus carrying Ukrainian Armed Forces servicemen and installed a camera to monitor the soldiers boarding the bus.

Is it a plane or a tree? Amelia Earhart expedition aims to solve mystery of disappearance
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:37:49 UTC
22:37:49 KST

A team of US researchers is approaching a remote Pacific atoll where they suspect the famed aviator Amelia Earhart crash-landed in 1937, in the latest attempt to crack one of the biggest mysteries of the 20th century.
The 17-person expedition was inspired by satellite images taken over several years showing a submerged object in the uninhabited island’s sandy lagoon – evidence dismissed by other longtime Earhart sleuths who say it is probably a fallen tree.
These researchers – led by archaeologists who raised funding from Earhart’s former benefactor, Purdue University – hope it will instead be revealed as the wreckage of her Lockheed Model 10-E Electra. Separate aerial footage of the area suggested the submerged object has a metallic glint, the team say.
“Finding Amelia Earhart’s Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime,” said the expedition’s leader, Richard Pettigrew, before he set sail this month. “Confirming the plane wreckage there would be the smoking-gun proof.”
Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan vanished during their attempt to circumnavigate the globe at the equator. By that point, Earhart, 39, was already a celebrity and aviation pioneer, having broken several records including being the first woman to make a nonstop solo transatlantic flight.
Locating the wreck of the twin-engine plane would confirm a long-held – but unproven – hypothesis that Earhart and Noonan ditched at the atoll of Nikumaroro, part of the archipelago country of Kiribati and about halfway between Australia and Hawaii.
They were en route to Howland Island, about 400 miles north of Nikumaroro, when their plane ran low on fuel and disappeared.
After a six-day sea voyage from Tarawa, the capital of Kiribati, the research group is expected to arrive on the uninhabited atoll on Tuesday local time and will spend several days searching for the “Taraia Object”, an elongated shape named after the part of the island where it was first noticed in a 2020 satellite image.
The expedition says it has been lying there for several years, and is even visible in aerial photography dating back to 1938.
Pettigrew, who heads the Archaeological Legacy Institute, a nonprofit organisation, raised funds for the mission with Purdue University in Indiana, where Earhart once taught and which funded her ill-fated final flight on the modified plane she called her “flying laboratory”. The university runs an airport and opened an Amelia Earhart Terminal last year.
The expedition builds on an already large body of evidence pinpointing the atoll as the location where the aviators went down. Much of it was gathered during dozens of visits between 1989 and 2019 by teams from the US explorers group Tigher (The International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery).
Tighar’s co-founder – and perhaps Earhart’s most well-known explorer – Ric Gillespie, said the Taraia Object was likely a dead pandanus tree, which is native to the area, that washed into the lagoon.
Gillespie, who is the author of One More Good Flight: The Amelia Earhart Tragedy, said he and other teams had visited the exact site where the object was located in 2001 and 2007 with metal detectors.
“There’s nothing there, or we would have found it,” he said in an interview this year. “If they suddenly discover that Amelia Earhart’s wreckage is there, I’ll be very surprised, but I’d be the first one to congratulate them. But I don’t think they are going to find anything.”
While Tighar agrees the Electra made an emergency landing on the atoll, they believe it was washed off a reef and now probably lies undiscovered and in pieces in deep water off the island’s western end.
Tighar’s version of the mystery was that Earhart, and possibly Noonan, were marooned on Nikumaroro but survived for a while, drinking rainwater and eating small fish and turtles. This theory is based on signs of a castaway’s campsite and 1930s-era artefacts, such as a jar of what is believed to be cosmetics freckle cream.
The pair’s disappearance led to a large US government search, including a flyover of Nikumaroro, then known as Gardner Island.
The Purdue mission says the object may not have been found by previous expeditions as it could have been covered with sand.

Nepal floods strand over 100 foreign trekkers, five villagers missing
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:36:36 UTC
22:36:36 KST

More than 100 foreign trekkers have been stranded in Nepal’s mountainous Gorkha district after flash floods swept away bridges and damaged trekking routes over the weekend.
Five villagers, including two women, remain missing after a landslide between Lokpa and Chumling blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering floods downstream, local news outlet Online Khabar reported on Monday, citing local authorities.
Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said four army helicopters were conducting rescue operations, with at least 47 people evacuated so far. A total of 437 security personnel had been mobilised.
The floods destroyed several bridges and damaged houses, two telephone towers and 50 electricity poles, the authority said.
No electricity
Md Shahadat Hossain, a Bangladeshi trekker stranded in Jagat village, said that nine Bangladeshis were awaiting possible helicopter evacuation.
“We have been stranded in Jagat since yesterday. A flash flood came down from above the village and flowed through its lower part,” he said.
He said more than 200 trekkers, including Nepalis, were sheltering safely in the village, but supplies were dwindling.
“We are safe, but there has been no electricity since yesterday, communication with the outside world has been disrupted, and food supplies are gradually running short,” he added.
The Manaslu Circuit, near Nepal’s border with China, is a popular Himalayan trekking route, with October among its busiest months.

When pilgrims became targets, billions could not save them
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:35:40 UTC
22:35:40 KST

The white ihram garments of Umrah pilgrims, stained crimson on the departure concourse of King Khalid International Airport. That image, seared into the global consciousness across the first weeks of October 2026, will define this moment for generations. It marks far more than a military operation; it is a definitive rupture in how the world understands power, vulnerability, and the fragile architecture of modern security.
What unfolded across 6–11 October was not merely a barrage of missiles and drones. A non-state militia emerging from one of the most impoverished regions on earth achieved what no conventional military force had accomplished in decades, piercing the multi-billion-dollar defensive shield of a G20 capital and bringing its flagship aviation hub to a standstill.
The multi-day bombardment killed at least 13 people and injured over 320, including pilgrims, international workers, and families with no connection to any political or military decision. Among the dead were Mohammed Yousuf, a 46-year-old Indian IT professional travelling with his family for Umrah, and Mufti Md Nasrullah Badrpur, a respected Bangladeshi Islamic scholar. These were not combatants. They were the guests of God.
This tragedy forces an urgent reckoning with a foundational doctrine of the modern state: that capital and technology can purchase absolute security. Riyadh constructed a defensive architecture of extraordinary sophistication: Patriot batteries, layered radar networks, advanced early-warning systems. The Houthis defeated it not through superior technology but through superior arithmetic.
Their layered assault combined low-altitude radar-evading cruise missiles, swarms of cheap suicide drones, and heavy ballistic missiles timed to exploit the window when defensive batteries were overwhelmed or reloading.
This is the buffer overflow doctrine: every defensive system possesses finite computational bandwidth, and when incoming threats exceed that capacity, the system collapses into paralysis.
The cost-exchange ratio is devastating. A single Patriot interceptor costs between three and four million dollars, with some estimates placing the PAC-2 GEM-T variant as high as four to six million dollars. A Houthi drone costs as little as $20,000 to $50,000, while a modified R-27 air-to-air missile repurposed for ground attack carries a conversion cost of roughly $20,000. This creates an exchange ratio sometimes estimated at eighty-five to one, according to analyses; the attacker needs to succeed only once to shatter the illusion of stability; the defender must be perfect one hundred per cent of the time.
As reported, Saudi Arabia is now running low on air-defence interceptors, shifting batteries around the country to protect palaces and energy infrastructure while seeking emergency assistance from Pakistan and other allies. This asymmetry represents the most significant strategic development since the advent of precision-guided munitions.
The ideological architecture behind Saudi statecraft, known as the ‘myth of impermeability’, was based on the notion that superior riches and Western defence technologies could create an inviolable island of hyper-modernity amid a chaotic area. The strikes exposed this as a dangerous delusion.
But something far more profound was also revealed: the targeting of pilgrims in ihram, individuals in a state of sacred purity entirely separated from worldly conflicts, represents a transgression that has unified the global Muslim community in unprecedented condemnation.
Al-Azhar Al-Sharif, the premier seat of Sunni Islamic learning, issued a binding fatwa classifying the attack as Hirabah, a crime of waging war against society and divine order, effectively stripping the perpetrators of any religious legitimacy.
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation has condemned the targeting of Makkah-bound pilgrims as an affront to Islamic values, emphasising that the safety of pilgrims is a sacred red line that must transcend any geopolitical conflict. As coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki declared, the security of the Two Holy Mosques and the safety of pilgrims remains a red line.
The economic implications for Saudi Vision 2030 are equally severe. National carrier Saudia was forced to cancel seventy per cent of scheduled departures from Riyadh. Flights at the airport were reduced by approximately eighty-five per cent as of 11 October. The nascent flagship carrier Riyadh Air paused its operations entirely. Global carriers including Emirates, Etihad, and Qatar Airways suspended hub connections.
The strikes occurred on the eve of the World Petroleum Council Energy Congress and weeks before the Future Investment Initiative events where billions in foreign direct investment were to be secured for the kingdom’s transformative agenda.
BP CEO Meg O’Neill and Shell CEO Wael Sawan both notified organisers they could not attend due to flight disruptions. The Clingendael Institute has assessed that Vision 2030’s core assumptions attracting foreign investment, competing with the UAE, and prioritising sectors like AI and tourism are threatened by wartime physical, economic, and political damage. The lesson for global investors is stark: no amount of sovereign wealth can guarantee the physical security upon which economic continuity depends.
The international response has been remarkable. The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, representing pilgrim-sending nations including Indonesia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, and Turkey, has moved rapidly to establish a Sacred Corridors framework, a diplomatic initiative to designate all transit routes for religious pilgrimage as permanently demilitarised zones under international protection.
This represents an extraordinary innovation in international humanitarian law, expanding the concept of protected spaces from fixed properties to dynamic transit vectors. The proposal would move through a UN General Assembly resolution to establish broad consensus, followed by a Chapter VII Security Council mandate to make the protection binding and enforceable.
For the United States, the strikes present a strategic dilemma of profound consequence. President Trump has confirmed that Washington is evaluating direct military action against Houthi infrastructure following the death of an American citizen. Yet Washington has so far resisted Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s requests for military help to roll back Houthi advances in Yemen, though it has sent military advisers.
The argument for diplomatic enforcement rather than kinetic escalation grows more compelling by the day. The security of the Two Holy Mosques, revered by over a billion Muslims worldwide, cannot be guaranteed through military means alone. The sanctity of Makkah and Madinah demands a political settlement that addresses the underlying regional conflicts driving this escalation.
The Houthis themselves are no longer second- or third-tier members of Iran’s Axis of Resistance, as RAND analysts have observed. While they benefit from Iranian weapons, training, and know-how, they also have their own interests at heart and behave accordingly. They are in a position to shape the next phase of the conflict between the United States and Iran, and they control a choke point at the Bab al-Mandeb through which twelve to fifteen per cent of maritime trade travels. This is not a proxy that can be controlled; it is an autonomous actor with strategic reach.
The Riyadh strikes have definitively ended the era of localised warfare. Geographic distance no longer guarantees safety. A militia operating from one of the world’s poorest nations can now directly disrupt the economic continuity of a global superpower.
The hub-and-spoke model that underpins modern globalisation the concentration of value in single nodes of maximum efficiency has revealed itself as a single point of failure. As researchers have demonstrated, critical infrastructure networks exhibit complex interdependencies that can lead to cascading failures with catastrophic consequences, where single-node disruptions propagate rapidly due to structural dependencies and high-impact linkages.
The implication for the global community is unmistakable. Security in the twenty-first century cannot be purchased through technology alone. It requires political stabilisation, diplomatic engagement, and the construction of new legal architectures capable of protecting the innocent from the cruel arithmetic of asymmetric conflict.
The blood on those white garments demands nothing less. The question is not whether the world will learn these lessons, but whether it will act before the next illusion of security is shattered.

Tiger that mauled man to death will not be euthanized, says UK wildlife park
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:35:22 UTC
22:35:22 KST

Rabia Ali
12 October 2026•Update: 12 October 2026
A private wildlife park in northern England said that a tiger that mauled a man who entered its enclosure would not be euthanized.
In a social media statement on Sunday, the Yorkshire Wildlife Park said the tiger, named Altai, was “safe and well and will not be euthanised as a result of this incident.”
The park also expressed sympathy for the man’s family and said staff members affected by the incident would get specialist support.
The park remained closed Monday as police continued investigating the incident, which took place on Saturday.
South Yorkshire Police said on its official website that officers received reports after midday on Saturday of a man entering a tiger enclosure.
“The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury,” police said, adding that the man was pronounced dead at the scene despite efforts by emergency medical personnel.
Police said the man’s family was getting support from specialist officers.
The force also said the tiger was uninjured and remained inside the enclosure, adding that there was “no wider risk to the public.”
South Yorkshire Police urged the public not to share footage of the incident circulating online, calling it distressing.
The privately run park opened in 2009. Its Land of the Tigers attraction opened in 2011 and includes a two-acre reserve for Amur tigers, also known as Siberian tigers, an endangered subspecies with an estimated 500 remaining in the wild.

IN BRIEF: EU add about 1,600 companies, individuals to anti-Russian sanction list
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:35:10 UTC
22:35:10 KST

MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. The European Union approved the 22nd package of anti-Russian sanctions and blacklisted about 1,600 companies and individuals related to the defense sector, EU diplomacy chief Kaja Kallas said on X.
TASS has collected key details of new restrictions.
Scale
- The EU expanded the special designations list against Russia from 3,100 to 4,700 position, according to the Council Resolution posted on the Official Journal of the EU.
- Sanctions were imposed in total on 826 companies and 743 individuals, mainly businessmen and officials associated with the Russian defense sector.
- The EU blacklist accordingly grew up by 1.5 times.
- All the persons in the list are banned from entering the EU, their assets should be frozen in the EU, and EU companies and individuals are debarred from having any relations with them.
Individuals
- The EU Council added to its sanction list 77 participants in elections to the State Duma in Crimea, Donbass and Novorossiya, including candidates and elected parliament members.
- The EU included in the 22nd package of sanctions CEO of the Middle Neva Shipyard Sergey Karachkov, President of Black Horse holding Vladimir Sokolov, CEO of the 81st Armor Repair Plant Vladimir Belakin, ex-CEO of the Krylov State Research Center Dmitry Novikov, head of the Special Design Bureau of the Russian Defense Ministry Denis Gorsky, CEO of the United Rocket and Space Corporation Sergey Gureev, CEO of the Russian Space Systems Dmitry Avtaikin and CEO of the State Munition Test Ranges Stanislav Yuzov.
- Restrictions were also introduced against President of the Russian Academy of Missile and Artillery Sciences Vasily Burenok
- The EU added former acting Prime Minister of Ukraine Gennady Arbuzov to its sanction list as well.
Organizations and companies
- The EU added UDC-Gas Turbines gas turbine equipment producer into the sanction list.
- Restrictions were also introduced against UDC-Perm Motors, the engine producer for civil and transport aviation and commercial gas turbines.
- Russian tire holding Cordiant was blacklisted.
- Sanctions were imposed on Samolyot developer and its CEO Anna Akinshina.
- The Gaz Automobile Plant was added to the designation list.
- Sevmash, Zvezda and Rybinsk Shipyards were hit by sanctions.
- Sanctions were expanded to cover Russian producers of IT solutions and microelectronics, as well as apparel factories.

EU foreign ministers on Monday formally adopted the bloc’s largest-ever expansion of its Russia sanctions blacklist, targeting nearly 1,600 people and companies linked to the country’s military-industrial complex.
The measures, initially agreed by EU envoys last week, add 826 Russian companies and 743 executives to the blacklist.
“Over half address the production chain for the ballistic missiles Russia uses to kill Ukrainian civilians every day,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said.
The companies supply components for Russian missiles, drones and aircraft, including explosives, ammunition, semiconductors and computers, according to the EU.
The bloc said they represent the “core” of the Russian military industry, employing more than a quarter-million people and generating an annual turnover of at least 20 billion euros ($22.3 billion).
The EU also sanctioned 74 State Duma lawmakers and three members of Russia’s Central Election Commission over their involvement in parliamentary elections held in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories.
Separately, three people and four entities in North Korea were sanctioned over Pyongyang’s growing military and economic cooperation with Moscow.
Those listed face EU asset freezes, while EU citizens and companies are barred from making funds available to them. Sanctioned individuals also face travel bans across the 27-member bloc.
The latest additions bring the total number of people and entities under EU sanctions over Russia’s war in Ukraine to nearly 4,600.

Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a Rome hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a lung nodule that was discovered during a routine medical checkup, the Vatican said Monday.
The Vatican said the nodule was not linked to symptoms such as inflammation or infection. The American-born pontiff announced during his Sunday Angelus address that he would have the operation in the coming days.
Holy See spokesman Matteo Bruni said Leo was following his schedule as planned on Monday ahead of the procedure.
The surgery will take place at Rome's Gemelli hospital, which treated popes from St. John Paul II – whose pontificate lasted from 1978 to 2005 – onward. The Vatican said the pope is expected to need about a week to recover.

Lebanon explosives seizure revives fears of political killings
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:33:04 UTC
22:33:04 KST

Breadcrumb
Seizure of explosives in Lebanon revives fears of political assassinations
The seizure of nearly half a tonne of explosives in Lebanon has reignited fears of political assassinations and intensified tensions over Hezbollah's weapons, amid conflicting reports about the shipment's intended use.
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam vowed on Monday that there would be "no tolerance or turning a blind eye, but truth and accountability", pledging to pursue everyone involved in the case.
Security forces arrested two men several days ago in Dahr al-Baidar, on the main road connecting the Bekaa Valley to Beirut, after discovering the explosives in their vehicle. The suspects are believed to have links to Hezbollah, although neither the group nor security authorities have issued an official statement on the incident.
Conflicting media reports have suggested that the detainees admitted to transporting the shipment on Hezbollah's orders to Beirut's southern suburbs, while other accounts claimed they had not acknowledged the group's involvement or identified the intended recipient.
Judicial sources told The New Arab that numerous inaccurate accounts were circulating.
"The case is sensitive and is being followed up in coordination between the various agencies. The investigations will continue until the end, and it is unacceptable to prejudge their outcome," the sources said.
They added that investigators were pursuing names mentioned during the suspects' initial questioning but declined to confirm reports implicating two Hezbollah commanders.
Salam praised the security forces for intercepting the shipment, acknowledging public concerns given the use of C-4 explosives in several political assassinations in Lebanon's recent history.
He pledged to identify those responsible and their motives, warning that his government would act firmly against weapons possessed, transported or used outside state authority.
Justice Minister Adel Nassar similarly said efforts to disarm unauthorised groups, combat terrorism and prosecute lawbreakers were irreversible.
Hezbollah defends armed resistance
Hezbollah MP Ibrahim Mousawi defended the group's activities on Monday, saying that if the vehicle belonged to the group, it would have nothing to hide.
"If it is true that the vehicle belongs to the resistance, everyone should know that the resistance is neither ashamed nor embarrassed, and carries out its duty openly," he said.
Mousawi argued that Hezbollah had a legitimate right to resist Israel's continued occupation and attacks on Lebanon, particularly while the Lebanese army lacked the equipment and political backing to confront Israel.
He also rejected suggestions linking the shipment to potential political assassinations, describing such accusations as unacceptable and insisting Hezbollah had avoided internal conflict even when it was at the height of its military strength.
Fears of renewed assassinations
The seizure has revived memories of Lebanon's wave of political assassinations between 2004 and 2008, which targeted prominent politicians, journalists and security officials opposed to Hezbollah and the Syrian government. Many of the killings remain unresolved.
Lebanese Forces leader Samir Geagea described the incident as the most dangerous security development in years, questioning why the explosives were being transported towards Beirut rather than southern Lebanon if they were intended for use against Israel.
Kataeb Party leader Sami Gemayel drew parallels with the 2005 assassination of former Prime Minister Rafik Hariri.
"In 2005, the truck carrying explosives was not intercepted, and the result was the assassination of Prime Minister Rafik Hariri," he wrote on X.
Gemayel warned of a possible new wave of assassinations and urged the government to dismantle Hezbollah's military and security infrastructure.
Independent MP Yassin Yassin also called for all weapons to be brought under state control, warning against waiting for another assassination before taking action.
Meanwhile, MP Ashraf Rifi demanded a comprehensive investigation into the shipment's origins, destination and intended use, including any possible links to previous political assassinations.
The controversy comes as Lebanese security forces intensify operations against weapons and drug smuggling along the Syrian border.
In recent weeks, authorities have intercepted shipments including 245 kilograms of TNT, explosive devices and detonators.
On Friday, the Lebanese army announced that it had foiled another attempt to smuggle rocket-propelled grenades, explosives and drugs from Syria into Lebanon, during an operation involving an armed confrontation with a suspected smuggler.

In Odesa Oblast, a one-month-old boy died of starvation — his mother is under arrest, and an official has been served with a notice of suspicion

Unknown Publisher

16:32:00 EEST
22:32:00 KST

In Odesa Oblast, a one-month-old boy died of starvation — his mother is under arrest, and an official has been served with a notice of suspicion
Kyiv • UNN
The child died due to inadequate nutrition and care. The official is accused of official negligence, while the mother is under house arrest.
The head of the Children’s Services of one of the districts in Odesa region has been served with a notice of suspicion over the death of a one-month-old child from starvation. As reported by the Prosecutor General’s Office, the official knew about the children’s inadequate living conditions but failed to take timely measures to protect them, reports UNN.
Details
As reported by the Prosecutor General’s Office, back in June 2025, an inspection found that the 23-year-old mother was failing to properly care for her three sons, aged 4, 3 and 1.5 years. Later, the woman stopped allowing social workers into the home.
The Commission for the Protection of Children’s Rights ordered that the boys be temporarily placed with a foster family. However, according to the investigation, the head of the Service failed to implement this decision in a timely manner.
In March 2026, the woman gave birth to her fourth son. The family was not provided with proper social support, and the infant’s safety was not assessed.
The boy did not receive adequate nutrition or care and was not under medical supervision. At the age of one month, he was hospitalized, but the child died. The causes were severe protein-energy malnutrition, developmental delay and nutritional deficiency. No diseases or congenital defects that could have caused the death were identified. According to the investigation’s findings, proper nutrition and care could have saved the child’s life.
Only after the infant’s death were his three brothers removed from the family. They are currently staying with a foster family.
The official is charged with official negligence resulting in a person’s death (Part 3 of Article 367 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine). The prosecution is seeking the suspect’s detention and suspension from office.
Separately, the court is considering the case against the children’s mother, who is accused of malicious failure to perform her childcare duties. She is under round-the-clock house arrest.

100 years of Bulgarian studies: Conference at Comenius University in Bratislava
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:31:37 UTC
22:31:37 KST

Author
Krasimir Martinov
News
100 years of Bulgarian studies: Conference at Comenius University in Bratislava
Slavic studies scholars from diffierent countries arrive in the Slovak capital for the anniversary
Monday 12 October 2026 15:25
Monday, 12 October 2026, 15:25
The building of the Faculty of Philosophy at Comenius University in Bratislava
PHOTO facebook.com/fphil.uniba
Font size
On 15 and 16 October, the Slovak capital, Bratislava, will host a major international academic conference dedicated to Bulgarian-Slovak cultural dialogue. On the evening of 15 October, the Bulgarian vocal quartet Svetoglas will give a concert entitled The Mystery of Bulgarian Polyphony.
Both the conference and the concert will take place at the Faculty of Philosophy of Comenius University in Bratislava. The occasion is a significant milestone: 100 years since the beginning of the academic study of the Bulgarian language at Slovakia’s largest and oldest university.
Celebrations marking the centenary of Bulgarian language teaching in Slovakia began back in September with the opening of two photographic exhibitions in the university’s Atrium art space. The first, Ancient Treasures of Bulgaria, was created by the Institute of Balkan Studies with the Centre of Thracology at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, with Prof. Valeria Fol and Dr Alexandra Milanova as its authors. The second, Bulgarian Monuments under UNESCO Protection, is a trilingual exhibition organised by the State Institute for Culture at Bulgaria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The exhibitions introduce students and visitors to significant archaeological discoveries, Thracian treasures and Bulgaria’s unique cultural and natural landmarks. These range from the world’s oldest worked gold, discovered in Varna, to Rila Monastery, Nessebar, the Boyana Church and the Madara Rider, as well as the natural beauty of the country’s national parks and reserves. The displays also feature striking photographs by renowned Bulgarian photographer Ivo Hadzhimishev.
The exhibitions will remain open until 15 October 2026, when the celebrations marking 100 years of Bulgarian studies in Slovakia will reach their climax.
H.E. Snezhana Yoveva-Dimitrova, Ambassador of the Republic of Bulgaria to the Slovak Republic, opens the exhibition
PHOTO facebook.com/Bulgarian.Embassy.Slovakia
The international academic conference Bulgarian-Slovak Intercultural Dialogue opens on 15 October. The two-day event is held under the patronage of Prof. Dr Marian Zouhar, Dean of the Faculty of Arts at Comenius University, and H.E. Snezhana Yoveva-Dimitrova, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Bulgaria to the Slovak Republic.
The conference boasts an exceptionally rich programme, organised into several panels running concurrently in different rooms of the Faculty of Arts at Comenius University.
The official opening at 9 am local time will be followed by a presentation by Slovak Bulgarian-studies scholar Prof. Maria Dobrikova, entitled Bulgarian Studies in Bratislava: A Century of University Education. Prof. Vladimir Penchev, a distinguished Bulgarian scholar of Slavic and Czech studies, ethnologist and researcher of the traditions and folklore of Bulgarian communities abroad, will present the findings of the first comprehensive study of the Bulgarian community in Slovakia.
On the first day of the conference, Mariola Walczak-Mikołajczakowa of Poland will present the Institute of Slavic Philology at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and its role in promoting Bulgarian culture, literature and language. Bulgarian-studies scholar Dr Maria Dudash of Hungary will then discuss the history of Bulgarian philology at Eötvös Loránd University in Budapest, while her colleague Monika Farkas Baráti will present Bulgarian studies at the University of Szeged. Svetlana Karadzhova, Bulgaria’s lecturer at the West University of Timișoara, will speak about the prospects for and challenges facing the study of Bulgarian in Romania.
The discussions will also address literary relations between Bulgaria and Slovakia, foreign-language teaching and other linguistic topics.
On the second day of the academic forum, 16 October, the scholars will pursue their discussions of topics including word formation, translation, phraseology, ethnolinguistics and history.
PHOTO Embassy of Bulgaria in Slovakia
Following the in-depth academic discussions at Comenius University, conference participants and official guests attending the centenary celebrations will have the opportunity to immerse themselves in the mystery of Bulgarian polyphonic singing with the Svetoglas quartet.
Founded in 2009 by Daniel Spasov and Milen Ivanov, both soloists with the world-renowned Mystery of Bulgarian Voices choir, the vocal quartet Svetoglas is one of Bulgaria’s distinguished ensembles dedicated to preserving and promoting the country’s ancient musical traditions. Through powerful polyphonic performances of authentic folk songs and Orthodox liturgical chants, the musicians reveal the richness, spirituality and beauty of Bulgaria’s musical heritage.
With its distinctive sound and original interpretation of tradition, the quartet has earned recognition both in Bulgaria and on the international stage. Svetoglas’s mission is to transform ancient musical messages into living art that resonates with contemporary audiences.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 12, 2026
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
21:31:27 CST
22:31:27 KST

Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will attend the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) held in Baku, Azerbaijan on October 15 as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping, and visit Azerbaijan, Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria from October 14 to 20.
Beijing Daily: Today, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs put on its website the decision to take countermeasures against Paraguay’s Minister of Information and Communication Technologies Gustavo Emigdio Villate Samaniego and Belize Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Francis Fonseca. Could you share more information on that?
Mao Ning: The Taiwan question is a major issue of principle bearing on China’s sovereignty and national reunification. It is at the core of China’s core interests. Certain politicians in Paraguay and Belize willingly serve as chess pieces for the DPP authorities in their pursuit of independence by soliciting external support. Their visits to Taiwan and reception of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces in their countries constitute severe interference in China’s internal affairs. They also attacked and smeared China by spreading the “Chinese cyber attack” disinformation, causing egregious impact in the world.
In response to these moves and in accordance with the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law of the People’s Republic of China, China announced in the form of MFA decree countermeasures as an action of warning and deterrence.
China News Service: Foreign Minister Wang Yi will attend the Seventh CICA Summit as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping and visit Azerbaijan. What’s China’s expectation of the visit?
Mao Ning: CICA is an important mechanism for security dialogue and cooperation in Asia. Since its inception, CICA has been committed to enhancing interaction and confidence-building among countries and made important contribution to security, stability and development in the region.
With growing complexity and volatility in the international and regional landscapes, Asian countries are increasingly keen to ensure peace and tranquility and promote economic growth. At the upcoming summit, China will engage in extensive dialogue and consultation with various parties to practice multilateralism, actively implement the four global initiatives, and enhance Asian governance, so as to make new contribution to building an Asian community with a shared future.
China and Azerbaijan are comprehensive strategic partners. In recent years, under the strategic planning and guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Ilham Aliyev, China-Azerbaijan relations have maintained strong momentum of growth, with ever-deepening political mutual trust, steady progress in Belt and Road cooperation and fruitful collaboration on international affairs. This will be Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s first official visit to Azerbaijan in seven years. He will hold talks with Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov. We believe the visit will help fully implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state and deliver new outcomes for bilateral cooperation across various fields.
AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia on Sunday. The ceasefire was met with surprise from Kiev and silence from Moscow and appeared shaky as Russia appeared to strike multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this “energy ceasefire”?
Mao Ning: China’s position on the Ukraine crisis is consistent and clear. We believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out, and support all efforts conducive to peace.
Reuters: The U.S. State Department last week said China’s maritime activities off Taiwan’s east coast are “deeply destabilizing.” What is the foreign ministry’s comment on that?
Mao Ning: China has on multiple occasions made clear its position on this. China has exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in waters east of the Taiwan island. It is fully within China’s sovereign rights and jurisdiction, therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach, for China to carry out activities in these waters. The party that instigates troubles and disrupts stability in this part of waters has never been the Chinese side.
The Taiwan question is China’s internal affair that brooks no external interference. The U.S. needs to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, handle the Taiwan question prudently, and take concrete actions to uphold the overall China-U.S. relations and peace and stability in the region.
Xinhua News Agency: On October 10, leader of the Taiwan region Lai Ching-te made a speech in which he again solicited external support for “Taiwan independence,” and smeared Chinese mainland. What’s your comment?
Mao Ning: There is but one China in the world. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory, and the Government of the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. To uphold the one-China principle, reject “Taiwan independence” separatist activities and support China’s reunification is where international public opinion trends.
Lai Ching-te’s so-called “democracy” cannot hide his “Taiwan independence” separatist nature. Taiwan’s return to China is an integral part of the outcome of WWII victory and the postwar international order. The real status quo across the Taiwan Strait is that both sides of the Strait belong to one and the same China. Whatever Lai Ching-te says or does, it does not change the fact backed by history and law that Taiwan belongs to China or the doomed failure of “Taiwan independence,” and will by no means stop China’s ultimate reunification.
CGTN: Could you elaborate on the program and China’s expectation of Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s visit to Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria?
Mao Ning: Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria are China’s important cooperation partners in Southeastern Europe. In recent years, China has maintained close exchanges with the three countries. Notable results have been achieved in cooperation on economy and trade, investment, tourism and infrastructure. There is extensive common ground on safeguarding multilateralism, tackling global challenges, growing China-Europe relations and other topics. During the visit, Foreign Minister Wang Yi will hold talks with the foreign ministers of the three countries and have in-depth exchange of views with their leaders.
Croatia is China’s important partner in the EU. The Chinese-built Pelješac Bridge is a landmark project of China-Croatia and China-EU cooperation. The two countries have enjoyed a more mature and stable partnership of comprehensive cooperation. Through the visit, China looks to better synergize development strategies and expand practical cooperation with Croatia, so as to promote the steady and sustained growth of bilateral ties.
This year marks the 20th anniversary of China’s diplomatic relations with Montenegro. Throughout those two decades, the two sides have always treated each other with respect and as equals. Together, the two countries have built a series of landmark projects, such as the South-North Expressway in Montenegro. China hopes that through the Chinese foreign minister’s first visit, the two sides will expand the breadth and depth of mutually beneficial cooperation, carry forward the traditional friendship, and inject new impetus into bilateral relations for the next 20 years.
Bulgaria is the second country in the entire world to establish diplomatic relations with New China. In recent years, China-Bulgaria strategic partnership has grown steadily, with close high-level exchanges and fruitful outcomes of practical cooperation. Through this visit, China looks to cement mutual trust, advance cooperation and deepen friendship with the new Bulgarian government, so as to further advance and deepen bilateral ties.
Reuters: Regarding China’s sanctions on the Paraguay and Belize ministers, would this be first of such measures against ministers from countries that maintain ties with Taiwan?
Mao Ning: For diehard supporters of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, China will take all necessary punitive measures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge the very few countries left which still have so-called “diplomatic ties” with China’s Taiwan region to avoid being repeatedly manipulated and used by separatist forces for “Taiwan independence.” Betting on “Taiwan independence” has no future. It will only cost them opportunities for development and lead to international isolation.
Global Times: Following his recent visit to China, former Japanese Foreign Minister and head of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade Mr. Takeshi Iwaya said that the deterioration in China-Japan relations was caused by the Japanese side and that the Japanese government should seek ways to improve the bilateral ties. There are voices in Japan criticizing the evasion of historical responsibility for leading astray Japan’s policy toward China, and calling on the Japanese government to face up to and address the wrongdoings. What’s China’s comment?
Mao Ning: China commends these remarks, which reflect reason and conscience among those with insight in Japan. As they have pointed out, the real issue lies in the distorted and erroneous views toward history and China held by those running the Japanese government, which has severely undermined the political foundation of China-Japan relations. The situation does not serve the two countries’ interests, and the responsibility rests fully with Japan. To bring China-Japan relations back to the right track, the ball is, apparently, in Japan’s court.
We urge those running the Japanese government to heed and take seriously the just voice at home, face up to the root causes of the problem, abide by the four political documents between China and Japan, and genuinely reflect on and correct wrongdoings on such issues as Taiwan, the history, and their China perception.
AFP: A fresh Houthis strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 11 others. This comes a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group. Can the Chinese foreign ministry comment on this?
Mao Ning: China condemns the attacks, which caused significant casualties, and expresses grave concern over the escalating conflict. China opposes attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We urge the parties concerned to refrain from actions that could further escalate regional tensions, resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and negotiations, and work toward peace and stability in the region at an early date.
Shenzhen TV: Today is the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Papua New Guinea. How does China see the development of bilateral ties over the past 50 years? What’s China’s expectation moving forward?
Mao Ning: Today marks the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between China and Papua New Guinea. President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang have respectively exchanged congratulatory messages with Governor-General Bob Dadae and Prime Minister James Marape. As President Xi pointed out in his congratulatory message, over half a century since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, conducted fruitful cooperation for mutual benefit, and expanded people-to-people exchanges. The remarkable progress in bilateral relations has not only benefited the two peoples, but also injected strong momentum to building a community with a shared future between China and Pacific Island countries.
China stands ready to work with Papua New Guinea to jointly implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders, carry forward our traditional friendship, and strengthen exchanges and cooperation across the board, so as to elevate our comprehensive strategic partnership to new heights and build an even closer community with a shared future between China and Pacific Island countries.
Reuters: There was a landslide in Nepal’s Gorkha district that led to the downstream flooding in the Budhi Gandaki river. This area is part of a major trekking route. Were there any Chinese nationals affected by the flood?
Mao Ning: We have no information on Chinese casualties for the time being. We extend sympathies to Nepal, and will provide assistance within our capacity in light of Nepal’s need.
AFP: The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court, vowing to cripple its operations just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize went to a former ICC judge. I wonder if China has a comment on this.
Mao Ning: We noticed the developments. China is not a state party to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. China’s position on relevant issues is consistent.
AFP: South Korea’s military said that North Korea on Monday fired multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on this.
Mao Ning: We notice relevant reports, and have no comment to add.
Reuters: There have been youth-led protests happening in Delhi over the weekend and in several other cities in India as well, calling for the resignation of India’s election chief. Will China consider issuing any travel advisories against visiting Delhi or any part of India in the near future?
Mao Ning: China noted the developments, and will assess whether advisories are needed as the situation evolves.

Police swooped on Renoir theft suspects fearing second museum heist, prosecutor says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
13:30:47 UTC
22:30:47 KST

Police swooped on Renoir theft suspects fearing second museum heist, prosecutor says
NANTERRE, France, Oct 12 - French police accelerated the arrest of suspects in a theft of two Renoir paintings after one of the alleged thieves visited another museum, raising fears of an imminent second theft, Marseille prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said on Monday.
Police arrested six suspects earlier this month and four men have since been charged. The two men suspected of carrying out the theft were charged with organised theft and other offences.
A third man, accused of hiding the paintings, was charged with organised handling of stolen goods. A fourth suspect, who investigators say was approached about buying the artworks, was charged with handling stolen goods and taking part in a criminal conspiracy.
PAINTINGS WORTH MORE THAN €4 MILLION
The stolen works, "Madame Colonna Romano" and "Young Woman at the Well" by Impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir, were valued at about €4.2 million ($4.7 million), Bessone said.
The theft took place on September 8 at the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, on the French Riviera. According to investigators, the thieves entered the museum grounds through a hole cut in a garden fence and got inside through a window.
The paintings were later found hidden behind a false wall in a house.
Both works were damaged and will need restoration. One of the paintings, "Madame Colonna Romano", had been torn.
The recovery came almost exactly one month after the theft, following an investigation that used DNA evidence, mobile phone geolocation data and surveillance footage.
Bessone said the suspects had denied planning a second museum raid, but he added that he did "not believe the principal suspect visited that museum simply out of a love of art".
The thieves also attempted to steal two other Renoir paintings, "Madame Pichon" and "Coco Reading", which depicts Renoir's young son Claude. They abandoned those works in the museum gardens while fleeing police who had arrived at the scene. ($1 = 0.8945 euros) REUTERS
